p: Save some neck strength for the Heaven Room. Painted by the Italian artist Antonio Verrio in the late seventeenth century, it's covered from floor to ceiling with gods and goddesses tumbling out of the walls, and it's one of those rooms that makes everyone stop and stare. It's often a highlight of the whole tour, so take your time and enjoy the detail.

Burghley has had plenty of screen time too. It appeared as Rosings Park in the 2005 film of Pride and Prejudice and as Castel Gandolfo in The Da Vinci Code, which gives film fans a bit of extra fun as they explore.

Out in the park, look for the herd of fallow deer grazing under the old trees. They're used to people but are wild animals, so keep a respectful distance, especially during the autumn rut and when there are young about in early summer. Dogs should be kept on leads where signs ask.

Each year, late summer brings the Burghley Horse Trials, one of the big events of the eventing calendar, with top riders tackling the cross-country course in the park. It draws huge crowds, so if you're visiting the house around then, expect busier roads and plan your timing carefully.

Stamford itself is a delight to explore on foot. Its golden stone streets have appeared in period dramas, including the BBC's Middlemarch, and the historic George Hotel is a lovely spot for a drink. Combine a morning at Burghley with an afternoon in town and you've got a very handsome day out.
